title: The diamond problem and default-method conflict resolution
answer: The diamond problem occurs when a type could inherit competing implementations of the same member through multiple inheritance paths. Java avoids multiple inheritance of classes, but two interfaces may provide the same default method. In that case the implementing class must resolve the conflict explicitly. AeroTopo's `Units` implements both `Left` and `Right`, each defining `units()`, and overrides `units()` to choose `Left.super.units()`.
